source_caption:
Pixar brilliantly encapsulates the entire existential weight of the film into a brief, profoundly simple parable about a young fish looking for the ocean. When jazz legend Dorothea Williams shares this story with a quietly disillusioned Joe Gardner—just moments after he finally achieves his lifelong, defining dream—it masterfully shatters the dangerous illusion of the “arrival fallacy.” This quietly devastating revelation forces Joe to realize that genuine fulfillment isn’t a magical, elusive destination you finally reach, but rather the ability to recognize and appreciate the beautiful, ordinary water you are already swimming in every single day.
⠀
Soul (2020), directed by Pete Docter and Kemp Powers, starring Jamie Foxx, Tina Fey, Angela Bassett. A passionate middle school jazz teacher finally lands the gig of a lifetime, only to suffer a sudden accident that traps his soul in a mystical realm, forcing him to desperately reevaluate what truly gives human life meaning.

source_details.synopsis: Soul is a 2020 American animated fantasy film directed by Pete Docter, who co-wrote it with Mike Jones and Kemp Powers. Produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures, the film stars the voices of Jamie Foxx, Tina Fey, Graham Norton, Rachel House, Alice Braga, Richard Ayoade, Phylicia Rashad, Donnell Rawlings, Questlove, and Angela Bassett. It follows Joe Gardner (Foxx), a middle school teacher and aspiring pianist who falls into a coma following an accident and seeks to reunite his separated soul and body in time for his big break as a jazz musician.
